newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares off the starting blocks at top speed.
newsitem.headline: German shares off the starting blocks at top speed.

text.p: A powerful overnight performance on Wall Street and bullish dollar powered German shares to fresh heights on Thursday morning.
Volumes were high in early dealings, traders said, setting the scene for yet another firm rally.
"We are off like a rocket again," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"There has to come a time when people ask themselves why how long this frantic action can go on, but it doesn't look like today's the day."
The IBIS DAX index was trading up 40.81 points, or one percent, at 4,264.50 points at 0724 GMT.
September DTB DAX futures, having briefly popped over the psychologically key 4,300 point level, were up 38.50 points at 4,262.19.
Retailer Karstadt AG was the top performer of the day, hitting a high of 725 marks before settling back to 710 marks, up three percent.

Diverse speculation was circulating in the market about the company, including talk that it was a takeover target. Analysts are also upbeat about a pilot project running in one of its outlets designed to boost profits.
Karstadt rose six percent in bourse trade on Wednesday.

Chemical shares were also in the spotlight, boosted by the robust dollar, which was trading just below 1.80 marks on Thursday morning, despite attempts by the German government on Wednesday to calm the foreign exchange markets.
Bayer AG was trading heavily and up 1.42 marks, or 1.9 percent at 77.15 marks. BASF AG was up 1.10 marks at 72.45 marks.
The main early spur for the market was the surge on Wall Street which took the Dow Jones Index above 8,000 points for the first time.
Some dealers were dubious about the outlook for more gains.

A virtually uninterrupted rally has lifted the DAX 11 percent this month alone and the blue chip index has gained 45 percent this year -- an almost inconceivable performance given that some early forecasts for the year had set targets for the DAX of around 3,300 points.
"Everyone is talking about a correction. The problem is that nobody is selling," said a dealer.

At the same time, dealers noted that many of today's gains were driven by covering operations ahead of an expiry deadline on the DTB futures and options exchange tomorrow. That upped the chance of a correction kicking in on Friday.
